Monte Carlo Sensitivity Analysis for Sequential AIPE: Squared Multiple Correlation Coefficient

Source: R/seq_aipe_R2.R
seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity.Rd

Runs the sequential accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) procedure for the squared multiple correlation coefficient (seq_aipe_R2_pilot, then seq_aipe_R2 until the stopping rule is met) G times on multivariate normal data with a known population value, and summarizes the realized sample size, the realized confidence interval width, and the empirical coverage. Use it before a study to see what sample size to expect and how close the coverage is to the confidence level at the planned width and number of predictors: the procedure's guarantee is asymptotic, and its coverage falls, in some conditions far below the confidence level, as the number of predictors grows relative to the sample size the width calls for (see seq_aipe_R2, which attaches a note to an interval reported from fewer than \(p \max(20, 2p)\) observations; a design whose mean_n and median_n here are below that number is one in which a study will usually end with that note).

Usage

seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity(
  true_value,
  width,
  p,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  ci_method = c("wald", "log_transformed"),
  G = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  m_0 = p + 2,
  max_n = 100000L,
  batch = 1L
)

Arguments

true_value

The population squared multiple correlation coefficient under the data generating mechanism. A single number of at least 0 and less than 1.

width

The target full width of the confidence interval (\(\omega\) in the article). A single number greater than 0 and less than 1.

p

The number of predictors (\(k\) in the article). A whole number of at least 1.

conf_level

The confidence level (default 0.95).

ci_method

"wald" (the default) or "log_transformed", as in seq_aipe_R2.

G

The number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000). A whole number of at least 1.

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single whole number that set.seed() accepts to make the result reproducible; the caller's random number stream is then left as it was found.

m_0

The smallest pilot sample size allowed, passed to seq_aipe_R2_pilot. A whole number of at least p + 2, which is also the default.

max_n

The largest sample size a replication may reach: a replication in which the rule is still not met with max_n observations stops there. It must be at least the pilot sample size, and at least p + 3 with the log transformed interval (which is not defined with p + 2 observations). The cap is exact for any batch (the last batch is shortened).

batch

The number of observations added between checks of the stopping rule after the pilot sample (default 1).

Value

An object of class c("smsd_sensitivity", "data.frame"): a data frame with columns term and value, which can be used as any data frame and which prints its values in fixed notation. See smsd_sensitivity_methods for the print method. It has one row per summary, in this order:

true_value

The population squared multiple correlation supplied.

target_width

The target width supplied.

conf_level

The confidence level supplied.

replications

The number of replications run.

mean_n, median_n, sd_n

The mean, median, and standard deviation of the realized sample size. sd_n is NA when G is 1.

mean_width, median_width

The mean and median of the realized confidence interval width, over the replications that ended with an interval.

pct_width_within

The percentage (0 to 100) of replications whose realized width is at most the target.

coverage

The proportion (0 to 1) of replications whose interval contains true_value. A replication stopped by max_n at a check that has no interval (see seq_aipe_R2) counts as not covering and as not within the target width; this cannot happen with the data generated here.

pct_hit_max_n

The percentage (0 to 100) of replications stopped by max_n before the stopping rule was met (a replication in which the rule is met with exactly max_n observations is not counted). When it is above zero the other summaries are censored and should be read with care.

pct_variance_unusable

The percentage (0 to 100) of replications in which, at one or more checks up to the stopping point, the variance estimate was unusable: zero (a sample value of 0 or 1 to within the precision of the data) or not finite (see seq_aipe_R2). For the data generated here this is 0 in practice.

Details

Each replication draws \(p\) independent standard normal predictors and a response equal to \(\sqrt{\mathrm{P}^2 / p}\) times their sum plus independent normal error with variance \(1 - \mathrm{P}^2\), where \(\mathrm{P}^2\) is true_value. This is the design of the simulations in Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2019, p. 506). Under multivariate normality the distribution of the sample squared multiple correlation depends only on \(\mathrm{P}^2\), \(p\), and the sample size, so the results apply to any means, variances, and correlations among the predictors with the same population value.

The stopping rule is checked at the pilot sample size and then after every batch further observations. With batch = 1 this is the purely sequential procedure of the article; a larger value shows the overshoot to expect from a study that checks the rule only after every batch observations. The function gives the results that a loop of seq_aipe_R2 calls on the same observations would give, but it evaluates the rule from running sums, so a narrow target that needs thousands of observations per replication remains practical.

The function generates multivariate normal data only, the assumption under which the procedure is derived; see seq_aipe_R2 for measured coverage when that assumption fails.

References

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2019). Sequential accuracy in parameter estimation for population correlation coefficients. Psychological Methods, 24(4), 492–515. doi:10.1037/met0000203

Kelley, K. (2008). Sample size planning for the squared multiple correlation coefficient: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 43(4), 524–555. doi:10.1080/00273170802490632

See also

seq_aipe_R2, seq_aipe_R2_pilot; smsd_sensitivity_methods for how the result prints; in DMAR, ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity for the fixed sample size analog.

Other seq_aipe_R2: seq_aipe_R2(), seq_aipe_R2_pilot()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Francis Bilson Darku fbilsond@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# Three predictors, a population squared multiple correlation of .40, and
# a 95% confidence interval no wider than 0.25. G is small to keep the
# example quick; a reported analysis deserves G = 10000.
seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity(true_value = 0.40, width = 0.25, p = 3, G = 100,
                        seed = 113)
#> term                   value
#> true_value             0.4
#> target_width           0.25
#> conf_level             0.95
#> replications           100
#> mean_n                 143.38
#> median_n               148
#> sd_n                   13.39213
#> mean_width             0.2440061
#> median_width           0.2444849
#> pct_width_within       100
#> coverage               0.94
#> pct_hit_max_n          0
#> pct_variance_unusable  0

# The same study checking the stopping rule after every 20 participants.
seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity(true_value = 0.40, width = 0.25, p = 3, G = 100,
                        seed = 113, batch = 20)
#> term                   value
#> true_value             0.4
#> target_width           0.25
#> conf_level             0.95
#> replications           100
#> mean_n                 149.8
#> median_n               152
#> sd_n                   6.90191
#> mean_width             0.2401216
#> median_width           0.2419052
#> pct_width_within       100
#> coverage               0.93
#> pct_hit_max_n          0
#> pct_variance_unusable  0
